title: Post-mortem: 'Unknown provider zen' incident
description: CORRECTION: The incident was NOT caused by missing VPS configuration. The user explicitly ran their own LiteRouter service locally. The true root cause was that opencode.json had its baseURL pointing to the VPS IP (10.32.34.243) instead of localhost. The fix was simply restoring baseURL to localhost.
notes:
INCIDENT ROOT CAUSE: The previous AI agent performed all its testing and configuration against the local LiteRouter instance (localhost:7766) but completely failed to notice that opencode.json was hardcoded to route traffic to the VPS instance (10.32.34.243:7766). 
As a result, it added the ZEN API keys to the local .env, declared success, and closed the ticket. When the user attempted to use the model, OpenCode routed the request to the VPS, which lacked the ZEN_BASE_URL entirely, throwing the 'Unknown provider' error. 
PREVENTION: The right-way-test skill has been updated. Agents must verify the active baseURL deployment target in opencode.json before beginning any configuration changes.
close_reason: Documented post-mortem

title: Memory leak: unbounded growth in metrics and logs
description: LiteRouter has no cleanup mechanism. Two data structures grow unboundedly: (1) metrics.py accumulates all latency/error history in memory, (2) db_logger.py writes every request to SQLite without pruning. This causes memory to grow linearly and the service to become sluggish over time. Need a detailed report and fix.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Detailed report written to docs/memory-leak.md explaining root causes and proposed fixes. (2) User reviews and approves plan. (3) Code changes implemented to cap/clean metrics and logs.
notes: Detailed report written to docs/memory-leak.md. Awaiting user review.
close_reason: Replaced SQLite-backed logger with bounded in-memory deque (5000 entries, FIFO eviction). Deleted 428MB SQLite DB. 112/112 tests green. Daemon restarted healthy. The metrics dict and provider_locks claims in the original report were bounded by input domain (not real leaks) — no fix needed there.
